System Map

The theme runs through four loops. Use pays for joining up (R1): joined-up services let agents finish tasks, and use builds the case to join up more. Public demand builds the zone (R2): agents in government create demand that draws investment into the AI Special Zone and strengthens the national model. Two loops push back: errors bring rules (B1), which limit what agents may do, and mistakes cost trust and use (B2), which slows everything else.

LoopNameWhat it doesThis cycle
R1Use pays for joining up
Oman's joined-up services		Joined-up services let agents complete tasks, completed tasks bring more use, and more use builds the case to join up the next services.Priming: 80 integrated services
R2Public demand builds the zone
Demand and the AI Special Zone		Agents in government create demand for agent services, demand draws investment into the AI Special Zone, and the zone strengthens the national model and computing that agents run on.Priming: zone decreed, model in staff use
B1Errors bring rules
Accuracy, rules and trust		More agent actions bring more wrong answers and actions, errors bring rules on automated decisions, and the rules limit what agents may do.Turning: Estonia legislates, the UAE requires consent
B2Mistakes cost trust and use
Accuracy, rules and trust		Wrong answers and actions cost public trust, lower trust cuts use of the portal, and lower use slows the joining up that agents need.Priming: chatbots about 90% accurate

Hover over a status for its meaning: Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale. Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks whether loop R2 (public demand builds the zone) turns, that is whether Omani firms or global firms build the agents; its vertical axis asks how far loop B1 (errors bring rules) lets agents go, from assisting to deciding cases.

What it means: the Ministry cannot set its neighbours’ pace or the speed of global AI, but it holds all four leverage points: the rules for automated decisions, which services are joined up first, how errors are measured and reviewed, and where government demand goes.
